Title: Greater West London
Content:

Title: Bishops Stortford
Content:
Hi I’m Claire,

After leaving my secretarial job at a Stockbroker’s in London when I had my children, I began working at a local primary school which enabled me to be back in the workplace whilst still being able to be a full-time Mum – the holidays were an added bonus!

I began as a mid-day assistant and 10 years ago became a Higher Level Teaching Assistant (HLTA). The latter enabled me to take classes on my own and because of my love of art and craft I was always given the art and DT topics to do, which I and the children thoroughly enjoyed.  During my time at the school I had contact with many children with learning difficulties and autism, in particular working 1:1 with a child who had Down’s Syndrome, being involved with the planning of his lessons to enable him to access the curriculum – albeit at a much lower level.  This was very rewarding and although I stopped working with him once he went to secondary school, myself and another support assistant were invited to his 18th birthday party!

As both my children are now establishing their own careers, I decided it was time for a change. Creative Mojo has given me that opportunity whilst still being involved with arts and crafts. What more could I ask for!

I have now gone from working with the young, to the elderly.  It feels great to be able to give something back, re-kindle hidden creativity, turn “I can’t do it” into “I did it” and see smiling happy faces even just for a short time.

Title: Creative Mojo Bedford & District
Content: Hi there, My name is Joanne, but most people call me Jo. My link to all things creative started as a child and I was always playing and experimenting in the creative area while at school. I soon found my love for all things colourful and have not stopped since. As an adult, I have stayed in a classroom and trained as a teacher in South Africa. My experience in both Primary and Early Years has encouraged me to see that art is all about the process and not the product. Getting messy and enjoying the process is ok and quite a bit of fun too. The joy that a person finds while creating is irreplaceable and for that moment the world seems to stop! In my classes I hope to encourage and develop that joy of creativity - now in adults - by allowing them to build skills - whether familiar or untapped - using all sorts of artistic media. This improves the participants wellbeing and gives them a sense of pride and achievement after a larger piece has been completed. Some may choose to take a smaller piece with them, to remind them of their accomplishment and success, or simply to decorate a wall or shelf. Teaching adults and facilitating their learning in both groups and individually in a fun and engaging way is my aim and I hope to bring out the artist in them, if only for a short time. Let’s see what we can Create! "You can't use up creativity. The more you use the more you have." -- Maya Angelou

Title: Creative Mojo Belfast, Antrim, Banbridge, Craigavon & Dungannon
Content:
Helen brings over a decade of experience delivering engaging, inclusive art workshops in nursing care homes, day centers, sheltered housing, private homes, community groups, and children’s events. She has witnessed the profound benefits of art for people with dementia, mental health challenges, neurodivergence, learning disabilities, social isolation, and especially those who are severely disabled or non-verbal—using it as a gentle, powerful way to express emotions, memories, and needs beyond words.

With her calm, deeply compassionate nature and extraordinary patience, Helen creates safe spaces where participants join at their own pace, ensuring no one is left out or rushed. Her keen sensitivity to subtle non-verbal cues—gestures, expressions, body language, and artistic choices—helps her build genuine, trusting relationships quickly with residents and staff alike. Carers often praise her natural “way with her” highlighting how she motivates even the most withdrawn individuals to engage and thrive where others couldn’t, while always respecting care home routines, giving thoughtful feedback, and supporting the team’s efforts. This enables truly person-centred experiences that celebrate each person’s unique strengths and bring joy, trust, and connection.

Passionate about creativity’s transformative power, Helen joined Creative Mojo—a leading UK provider of high-quality art workshops for care and community settings—to access proven resources, innovative ideas, and a supportive network while expanding her reach. She loves sparking quiet connections with vulnerable adults and the pure fun of children’s groups alike. What excites her most is delivering more uplifting, reliable sessions that enhance wellbeing across care homes, families, schools, parties, and beyond.

In her free time, Helen finds inspiration in local history, walks, and gardening—keeping her creativity and appreciation for everyday beauty alive.
franchise_location_detailed: Belfast, Antrim, Banbridge, Craigavon & Dungannon
